This appeal having been heard and reserved for judgment  for pronouncement this day, JUSTICE AVANINDRA KUMAR SINGH  passed the following:

ORDER This appeal under section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 has been filed by the appellants/claimants against impugned award dated 30.9.2021 passed by Seventh Additional Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, Satna (for brevity "the Tribunal") in Claim Case No.128/2015 [Rajendra Gupta and another Vs. Daddi Rawat and 03 others] whereby the claim petition filed by appellant under section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 seeking compensation on account of death of deceased-Sitaram Gupta in motor accident dated 15.5.2018 occurred with offending insured Tractor bearing registration No.MP-19/AB-3886 has been dismissed.

entities.text: Seventh Additional Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, Satna
entities.label: COURT

entities.text: Rajendra Gupta and another Vs. Daddi Rawat and 03 others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 2. Being aggrieved with the impugned award passed by the Tribunal the appellants have filed this appeal on the ground that Tribunal has erroneously rejected the claim petition by observing the accident in question was not proved.
It has also been observed by the Tribunal that FIR does not disclose the registration number of the offending vehicle, though vehicle was involved in the accident.
It also does not disclose about the Doctor where the deceased was taken for treatment.
The other ground of dismissal is that the owner of the seized Tractor which cause accident is Janmejay Singh but in the FIR the name of owner is "Janmajor Singh".
In fact, it was default of subscriber of FIR for the appellant/claimant cannot be held responsible.
Therefore, prayer has been made to set aside the impugned award and grant compensation as prayed for.

3 . Learned counsel for the respondent No.4/Dharmvati Gupta submitted if eventually this Court arrives at a conclusion that appellants/claimants are entitled for compensation, then in that eventuality the respondent No.4 be granted compensation to the extent of one-third share.
4 . Perused the record of the Tribunal and considered the findings recorded by the Tribunal.
The FIR was delayed by more than a month.

Since registration number of the vehicle was not mentioned in the information to the Police or the Doctor when information for the first time was give,
therefore, it is a serious error especially in view of the fact that in name of Janmajor Singh, his father name was not mentioned.
If the name of father or place of residence like village, city, etc. would have been mentioned then it could have been held that it was a minor defect.
But, looking to the suspicious circumstances this is false case and the Tribunal has rightly rejected the claim of the appellants.
5. In the considered opinion of this Court the claim of the appellants h a s rightly been rejected by the Tribunal.
It is seen that suspicious circumstances have not been explained by the appellants.
It is not settled principle of law that in each and every motor accident case compensation has to be awarded, when the claimant has not satisfactorily proved the occurrence of accident.

It is to be Rajendra Gupta vs Janmejay Singh on 13 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/106844138/
2 considered that the Insurance Company has a duty to pay compensation only in respect to the rightful claims.
6. It is to be further noted that claimants have not with clean hands before the Tribunal.

sentences.text: When the claim petition was filed the claimants did not mention each and every fact fairly and clearly.
Both the appellants/claimants are sons of deceased-Sitaram Gupta.
They stated in the claim petition that their mother is dead.

But, subsequently it came to the knowledge of the appellants that one Dharamvati Gutpa was living as a wife of Late Sitaram Gupta and after the death of Sitaram Gupta she has received the amount of insurance policy.

Although subsequently said Dharamvati Gupta was impleaded as a party in the Tribunal, there was serious contest from the appellants/claimants that respondent No.4-Dharamvati Gupta should not be awarded the amount of compensation.
7. Besides above, it is also seen from the postmortem report that at that time the deceased was 66 years of age and he was filing income returns also.
But, in the claim petition it is mentioned that the deceased was 60 years of age.
It appears proper documents relating to age proof like 'Aadhaar' card etc. were deliberately withheld.

Further, the delay in FIR in claim case will not defeat the case but in FIR (Exhibit-P/2) it is mentioned in Column No.3 that accident took place on 15.5.2015 though there is correction in the date and such correction is not signed by any Police Officer.
This FIR was registered on the basis of Marg Intimation No.57/15 dated 17.6.2014 (Exhibit-P/4) under section 174 of Cr.P.C. wherein it is mentioned that date of accident is 24.5.2015.
The deceased expired in Metro Hospital, Gohalpur.

Exhibit-P/5 is the intimation by Metro Hospital & Cancer Research Centre, Jabalpur to Police Station, Gohalpur to the effect that patient expired on 24.5.2015 who was brought to the Hospital by Prafulla Gupta (nephew of deceased).

entities.text: Metro Hospital & Cancer Research Centre, Jabalpur
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: In fact the accident took place in front of Police Station, Rampur Baghelan and the house of the claimant is situated opposite side of Police Staion.
Hence, the delay in giving information o the Police cannot be countenanced.

8. From perusal of the evidence of Rajendra Gupta (AW.1) it is clear from paragraph 11 of the cross-examination that he had admitted that he was at shop and after accident they did not inform anyone as to how and who caused accident and whose vehicle was involved.
He stated that he does not remember that the report was lodged after one and half month of the date of accident.
He also admitted that in the FIR the registration number of the Tractor is also not mentioned, but name of owner is mentioned.
In paragraph 21 of his cross- examination he again admitted that in FIR (Exhibit-P/2) it is mentioned that accident was caused by Tractor of "Janmajor Singh".
He also agreed that in the claim petition "Janmajor Singh" is not a party.
9 . Pratul Gupta (AW.2) in paragraph 12 of cross-examination has admitted that at the time of accident i.e. 07 p.m. there was darkness at the place of incident.

Therefore, as in FIR (Exhibit-P/2)
the name of father of Janmajor Singh is not mentioned and Tractor Number is not mentioned,
whether Janmejay Singh s/o Bhoopal Singh r/o of Rampur Bagheln, District Satna is the registered owner of Tractor Number MP-19/AB-3886 and both (Janmejay & Janmajor) are one and same person can only be explained after examination of Investigating Officer, who had done the investigation or filed the charge-sheet.

Even otherwise, there is no explanation whether name of Rajendra Gupta vs Janmejay Singh on 13 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/106844138/
3 Janmajor Singh was mentioned due to some clerical mistake or they are two different persons.
10.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In fact, it is seen that appellants/claimants could have examined an Officer from the concerned R.T.O., to ascertain as whether the Tractor was registered in the name of Janmajor Singh of Satna.
The claimants not only should have led positive evidence but also negative evidence to rule out all possibility whether the tractor belongs to Janmajor Singh or Janmejay Singh.
This aspect is important as in Exhibit-P/10 (Mechanical Investigation of Tractor) which took place on 07.7.2015 due to late filing of F.I.R.
There is mention that Clutch, Brake, Steering, Head Light and Indicator are alright (OK).
There is no report that they have been repaired.

11 . In view of aforesaid analysis it is clear that the Tribunal has dealt with the factual and legal circumstances in all detail and this Court does not find it to be a fit case to interfere with the findings recorded by the Tribunal and take a different view.

12. In the result, the appeal being devoid of substance stands dismissed.
(AVANINDRA KUMAR SINGH) JUDGE RM Rajendra Gupta vs Janmejay Singh on 13 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/106844138/
